strategy.summary: Oberflächentechnik Weißacher is a founder-owned powder coater with 30 staff. It is our single source (100% quota) for part:330060, and it is in visible financial stress: credit index worsening, a credit downgrade after it paid its own suppliers late, a weak equity ratio, and a bank that reviews it monthly. Its managing director has said he cannot sign anything that lowers margin. The price has been flat at 9.99 since 2024, after an earlier cut. The current quote holds the price but asks for payment within 10 days. Its performance is poor and worsening: on-time delivery is far below the contract target, ppm runs at many times the peer median, and three 8Ds are open. We also pay it late, which is its main grievance. The currency here is cash and reliability of payment, not price. Trade on-time or 10-day payment and a 24-month commitment for a price hold or a small cut plus quality commitments (ppm target, higher chargeback). Do not squeeze margin on a fragile single source. We own the tooling, so a second source is possible in the long run, but none is qualified. Evidence on cost structure is thin: there is no should-cost, and the coating share is unindexed.

price_view.reasoning: There is no should-cost. Drivers support a modest increase, and it has already cut price and held flat for years. The MD refuses margin cuts, and its finances are weak. Any reduction must be bought with cash (payment speed) and commitment. A hold or a small cut is realistic; a deep cut is not.

strategy.writer_notes: Lead with cash: acknowledge our payment lapses, offer fast and reliable payment and a longer commitment, and ask in return for a price hold or a modest step plus a tight ppm commitment and a stronger chargeback. Keep quality and delivery records factual and use them to justify no increase, not to punish. Treat the supplier as a partner we want to keep healthy, and check on supply continuity. Hold back delivery and complaint records as fresh facts for later rounds.

findings.text: No should-cost exists for part:330060, so we cannot say how far 9.99 sits above full cost; the economics case rests only on driver indices and price history. Evidence on margin is thin.

Weighted driver movement over 12 months points mildly upward: labour +2.7% (w 0.34, ~+0.90%), steel PPI-C241 +6.5% (w 0.22, ~+1.44%), power -3.7% (w 0.07, ~-0.26%). Net about +2.1% on price for the 63% of cost covered; the remaining 37% (coating powder, other) has no index. A supplier claim of roughly +2% would be checkable and defensible; anything far above that is not backed.

Price has been flat at 9.99 since 2024 after a -6% cut from 10.63 (2023). Since that cut steel is still -6.3% below its 2023-08 peak and power -15% below 2024-11 peak, but these long-span comparisons are not checkable; only 12-month changes should be cited.

Current quote 7300070 holds price at 9.99 but asks payment within 10 days (vs contract net 30 / 2% skonto at 10). The supplier is cash-stressed (credit index 248->343, downgrade, MD says bank watches monthly, cannot lower margin). Price room is small; the real trade currency is payment timing: 2% skonto ≈20% p.a. to it, and our late payment (avg 7.9 days late) is a grievance we can fix.
Performance is poor (53.8% OTD, 5556 ppm vs peer 457), which argues against any increase and for chargeback/ppm terms rather than price cuts that would further weaken a fragile single source.
Contract fixes prices per calendar year with 90 days' notice before year-end (deadline ~2026-10-02); any 2027 increase must be notified in time.

Steel +6.5% and labour +2.7% give it a checkable ~+2% increase case
Our late payment undermines our position
No should-cost to test its margin

findings.text: Decision maker is the founder-owner managing director of a 30-staff GmbH. He is under bank scrutiny ('the bank is watching every month') and has said 'I cannot sign anything that lowers our margin now.' Any price cut that touches margin will hit a hard personal limit. Cash, not price, is the currency he responds to.

The supplier is in financial stress. Its credit index worsened from 248 to 343 in 12 months, and its equity ratio is 24.9%. A credit agency downgraded it on 2026-09-04 after it paid its own suppliers late. It is a supply risk because it is our single source with 100% quota, although we own the tooling.

Our own payment behaviour is a weak spot. 43.2% of invoices are paid late and 27% are more than 10 days late, with a maximum of 28 days. The supplier complained on 2026-08-20 ('overdue again… review our conditions'). The next day it offered a discount for payment within 10 days. Expect this grievance to come up early. Paying on time, or earlier, is the trade that gives it what it needs.

Its performance is poor, which weakens its position. On-time delivery is 53.8% against a 95% target, down from 59.3% a year earlier. Quality is 5,556 ppm against a peer median of 457 ppm, up from 1,423 ppm. There were 8 complaints, 3 of them without a closed 8D. The audit grade is C. The cause may be capacity or cash strain, so delivery and quality commitments are as relevant as price.

Its negotiation history is accommodating. It usually settles well below its ask, and the last renewal settled at +0.0%. The price has been flat at 9.99 since 2024. Under the contract, prices are fixed per calendar year and a change needs 90 days' notice. The renewal exit notice deadline is 2027-04-01.

Its style is polite but firm about formal terms. It plans ahead, for example asking for January call-offs by 10 December. We are a meaningful customer at about 6.2% of its turnover. The evidence on its cost structure is thin.

supplier_wants: Faster payment (within 10 days, with 2% skonto) and reliable on-time payment
No margin reduction while the bank is monitoring it
Timely call-offs before the holiday shutdown

Squeezing the price could break the managing director's margin limit and make him walk away; on a stabilise part this also adds a margin penalty
It may raise our late payment and 'review conditions' (tighten its terms)
Delivery and quality may deteriorate further
It may push a material-driven increase citing steel PPI +6.5%

findings.text: Framework agreement ctr:4600070350 covers only part:330060, runs 2025-07-01 to 2027-06-30 and auto-extends 12 months unless terminated with 90 days' notice (deadline 2027-04-01). Exit remains open, but it is only credible if a second source is qualified first.

Prices are fixed per calendar year. A change needs written notice at least 90 days before year end, i.e. by about 2026-10-02. Any increase request for 2027 must arrive by then, or the 9.99 price holds through 2027.

Payment is net 30 with 2% skonto within 10 days, and the Incoterm is DAP. Their 2% skonto implies cash is worth about 20% a year to them. Our own record is poor: we pay 7.9 days late on average and 43% of invoices are late. They complained about this on 2026-08-20 and asked for 10-day payment.

The quality clause sets a 95% on-time target and a EUR 150 flat fee per complaint. Performance is far below it: 53.8% on time and 5556 ppm from 8 complaints, against a peer median of 457 ppm. Only EUR 450 was recharged, and 3 complaints have no closed 8D. The flat fee does not deter.

Settlement history: 2024 asked -2.6%, settled -6%; 2025 asked +2.8%, settled 0; 2026 asked +1.9%, settled 0. They routinely settle 2-3 pp below their ask, and the price has been flat at 9.99 since 2024. Only three renewals, so the pattern is moderately reliable.

Dependency runs both ways. We are on a 100% single source with no other approved supplier and no RFQ history, but we own the tooling. Our roughly EUR 218k spend is about 6% of their turnover. Their health is weak: equity 24.9%, credit index rising from 248 to 343, a credit downgrade in Sept 2026, and the MD said he cannot sign anything that lowers margin.

findings.text: Delivery is poor and getting worse. Over the rolling 12 months to 2026-09 only 53.8% of deliveries were on time against our requested date, against a contract target of 95%. A year earlier it was 59.3%, and the peer median is 84.6%. Even against its own confirmed dates it reaches only 69.2%. Late lots average 17.5 days late, the worst was 40 days, and 6 orders needed rush lines. Note that requested and confirmed dates differ by a known 10-30 points, so cite the requested-date figure from the scorecard.

Quality has collapsed in 2026. Rolling ppm rose from 1,423 (2025Q3) to 2,218, then 3,850, then 5,556 (2026Q3), against a peer median of 457. The score fell to 49.1 (class C, red). Three QNs in Aug-Sep 2026 (coating defect, burr, leakage at test) still have no closed 8D, and their lots ran at 25,000-30,000 ppm.

The defects keep recurring rather than being fixed. 17 of 18 QNs on part:330060 were supplier-caused. Defect types repeat: wrong material certificate 3 times, leakage at test 3 times, dimension 3 times, porosity twice. 8D closure typically takes 2-3 months. Only EUR 1,650 has been recharged in total under the EUR 150 flat fee, because several QNs carried no recharge, so the fee does not cover the real cost of defects to us.

Volume is stable and slightly rising. The 2026-09 forecast, which is shared with the supplier, is 22,600 pcs for the next 12 months against 21,780 ordered in the last 12 months. That is about EUR 218k a year, or 6.2% of its turnover. For a weakened 30-person firm this volume is valuable, which gives us leverage to trade volume or commitment for performance terms.

The price has been flat at 9.99 since 2024, down 6% from 10.63 in 2023. The supplier can argue that it has already conceded on price and that steel and labour costs are rising. With its finances strained, a further price cut risks its supply; better levers are payment terms and quality commitments such as ppm targets and a chargeback per complaint.

The supplier's case: we pay late, 43% of invoices and 7.9 days late on average, and it is asking for faster payment. Its credit index worsened from 248 to 343. It is also our single source with a 100% quota, although we own the tooling.

arguments.text: Our price has not moved in three years while our costs have. We cut 6 % for 2024 (EV-2024) and then held 9.99 through two renewals in which we asked for +2.8 % and +1.9 % and settled at 0. In that time steel rose +6.5 % in 12 months and labour +2.7 %, and those two drivers are over half of the cost weighting. Holding 9.99 is already a real cut for us.

Hollerau pays us late. 43 % of invoices are paid late and 27 % more than 10 days late, by up to 28 days. That is our working capital financing Hollerau. Payment within 10 days, with the contractual 2 % skonto, is a fair and cheap fix. It is the one thing that makes holding the price possible.
We are your only qualified source, approved since 2020 and supplying since 1996. Requalifying a powder coater for the HB cover plate takes time and risk. Stable supply is worth more than a few cents.
The contract fixes prices per calendar year, and any change needs 90 days' notice before year end. 9.99 is the agreed basis, and we have honoured it.

Some of the late deliveries trace to how orders are placed: requested and confirmed dates differ by 10-30 points, there were 6 rush lines, and the holiday call-off requests were ignored. Measured against confirmed dates, our delivery is better.

weak_points: Quality is collapsing: ppm last 12 months is 5,556 against 1,423 a year earlier, and 3 open 8Ds from Aug-Sep 2026 have leakage, burr and coating defects.
On-time delivery is 53.8 % against the 95 % contract target, with up to 40 days late and 46 % of receipts late.

Our financial stress is visible: credit index has gone from 248 to 343, there was a downgrade for paying our own suppliers late, equity is 24.9 %, the bank monitors us monthly, and the MD said this on a call. Hollerau knows we need cash badly.
Hollerau owns the tooling, so resourcing is feasible.
Energy prices are falling (-3.7 % year on year).
We have no should-cost of our own to show, and the coating cost share is unproven.
Steel is still 26.7 % below its 2022 high.
wants: Payment in 10 days, or even shorter: for this I accept the 2 % skonto and hold 9.99.
A 24-month extension with binding volume of about 22,600 pcs a year, plus a better forecast and call-off discipline: for this I could consider a small cut of 1-2 % at most.
Prepayment or material advance for the steel.
red_lines: No price below 9.99 without faster payment, and no margin-cutting deal at all; the MD will not sign one.
No raised chargeback or an aggressive ppm penalty without a cash concession.
No longer payment terms than 30 days.
red_team.opening: Thank Hollerau for the long relationship, acknowledge the quality issues briefly and promise a corrective action plan. Then restate the quote: 9.99 held despite +6.5 % steel and +2.7 % labour, and three years of no increase. Ask, firmly but politely, for payment within 10 days with the 2 % skonto, pointing to the late-payment record. Offer the 24-month extension as an option. Do not mention the bank or the downgrade.

rebuttals.answer: You are right that the price has held flat after an earlier cut, and that steel and labour have risen; we do not dispute those drivers. Put in proportion, the weighted effect of those two indices on the part is modest, and power, another driver, has fallen over the same period. Your own earlier renewal asks were small and we settled them together. Holding the current price is therefore a fair outcome, not a loss, and we are ready to support it with terms that help you, rather than through an increase.

This is a fair complaint and we accept it: too many of your invoices have been paid late, and that is not how we want to treat a long-standing partner. We heard your request and your managing director's concern clearly. We are prepared to commit to fast, reliable payment, including payment within the discount period, as part of this agreement. In return we ask that the price holds or eases slightly and that we agree concrete quality and delivery commitments, so that both sides gain stability.

We value the long relationship and want you to remain our supplier for this part. Stable supply is exactly our concern, which is why recent delivery and quality results matter: on-time delivery is far below the contract target and the defect rate has risen sharply against both last year and the peer level. Security of supply comes from fixing those together, and we are offering cash speed and a longer commitment to help make that possible.

Agreed, the contract fixes prices per calendar year, the current price is the agreed basis, and we appreciate that you have honoured it. The same contract also sets the quality agreement and the on-time delivery target, which we would like to see honoured equally. We propose to keep the current basis and extend the commitment, combined with a clear quality target.

Some of this is fair: our ordering has not always been ideal, and we will respect your holiday call-off timing and reduce rush orders. Even measured against your own confirmed dates, however, a large share of receipts arrived late, and the trend has worsened over the year. We suggest we share firmer call-offs from our forecast and a binding volume, and that you commit to on-time delivery against the dates you confirm.

press: We would welcome a jointly agreed ppm target in the new agreement, since the defect rate over the past year has risen well above both your earlier level and the peer level.
We would like the on-time delivery target in our contract to become a shared commitment, supported by firmer call-offs from our side.
Since power costs have eased over the past year, we see the overall cost picture as balanced enough for the current price to hold.
As a counterpart to our faster payment, we would like to agree a complaint chargeback that better reflects the effort each defect causes us.
